texts.0: SP, due to a late transition from the instrument cross-check to the visual segment at the circling minimum descent altitude, did not hold the circling altitude during the downwind and base maneuvering. The aircraft descended more than 300 feet below the published circling altitude before it was in a position from which a normal descent to landing could be made. The IP intervened to arrest the descent and altitude control was not re-established by SP without assistance.
texts.1: SP, due to attention held on runway acquisition instead of the altimeter, allowed the circling altitude to erode to the 300 foot deviation limit while maneuvering visually. The deviation was arrested only after repeated verbal prompting from the IP, and the return to the published circling altitude was slow. No intervention on the controls was required.
texts.2: SP, due to a coarse power and pitch adjustment when rolling into the downwind turn, did not maintain the circling altitude precisely and the deviation reached the 150 to 300 foot band. SP recognized the trend on the next altimeter check, corrected with a small power change and returned to the published altitude promptly, without any prompting or intervention.
texts.3: SP held the circling altitude within 150 feet throughout the downwind, base and final maneuvering. Corrections were small and made early from the altimeter cross-check, and the aircraft remained at the published circling altitude until in a position for a normal descent to landing.
texts.4: SP flew the circling altitude with negligible excursions, well inside 150 feet and typically within a few tens of feet. Power and pitch were coordinated in both turns so that no correction was visible on the altimeter, and the published altitude was held precisely until the descent point.
texts.marginal: SP kept the circling altitude within standards, but the deviations sat close to the 150 foot band and were consistently low rather than distributed either side. The trend is a slow descent that begins in each turn and is caught late. SP is expected to anticipate the power requirement in the turn and to shorten the altimeter cross-check interval so that deviations stay clearly inside the tighter band.

texts_at.1: SP held the circling altitude with the deviation settling at the 300 foot limit, due to attention held on runway acquisition instead of the altimeter while maneuvering visually. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to keep the altimeter in the scan through the visual segment, not only the runway picture.
texts_at.2: SP held the circling altitude with the deviation settling in the 150 to 300 foot band, due to a coarse power and pitch adjustment when rolling into the downwind turn. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to make the power and pitch adjustment for the turn in a single coordinated action rather than in steps.
texts_at.3: SP held the circling altitude within 150 feet throughout the downwind, base and final maneuvering, due to one correction applied a beat after the deviation first showed rather than from the altimeter cross-check itself. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to act on the altimeter cross-check the instant a trend appears rather than a moment later.

texts_above.2: SP recognized the trend on the next altimeter check after the deviation reached the 150 to 300 foot band, corrected with a small power change and returned to the published altitude promptly, without prompting or intervention. Making the power and pitch adjustment for the turn in a single coordinated action, rather than in steps, would keep that deviation smaller. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to good altitude discipline in the circling pattern.
texts_above.3: SP held the circling altitude within 150 feet throughout the downwind, base and final maneuvering, with corrections small and made early from the altimeter cross-check. The only refinement available is to act on the cross-check the instant a trend appears rather than a moment later. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to very good altitude discipline in the circling pattern.
texts_above.4: SP flew the circling altitude with negligible excursions, well inside 150 feet and typically within about 30 feet, with power and pitch coordinated in both turns so no correction was visible on the altimeter. There is little left to refine; every turn is already flown with the power and pitch pre-coordinated. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to excellent altitude discipline in the circling pattern.

texts.0: SP, due to inadequate monitoring of airspeed during the approach, did not maintain the circling airspeed while maneuvering in the visual segment. Airspeed diverged by more than 20 knots from the target, with the excursion developing towards the low side during the base turn. The IP intervened with power to restore the required airspeed before the aircraft was aligned with the runway.
texts.1: SP, due to an interrupted instrument cross-check while attention remained outside on the runway, allowed the circling airspeed to reach the 20 knot deviation limit. Airspeed was recovered only after the IP called the deviation, and the correction was applied late and with an overshoot in the opposite direction. No intervention on the controls was required.
texts.2: SP, due to a delayed power reduction after configuring the aircraft, did not hold the circling airspeed exactly and the deviation reached the 10 to 20 knot band. SP detected the trend on the next cross-check, adjusted power smoothly and re-established the target airspeed before the base turn, with no prompting or intervention.
texts.3: SP maintained the circling airspeed within 10 knots throughout the maneuvering, including through the configuration change and both turns. Power corrections were small and anticipated, and the aircraft was on speed when established on final.
texts.4: SP flew the circling airspeed with negligible variation, well inside 10 knots at all points of the pattern. Airspeed remained stable through the configuration change and both turns and required only minimal power adjustment.
texts.marginal: SP remained within the airspeed standard, but the deviations clustered near the 10 knot band and recurred at the same point in the base turn. The trend is a fast entry that is bled off late on final. SP is expected to set the required power earlier in the turn and to keep the airspeed indication in the cross-check so that variation stays clearly inside the tighter band.

texts_at.1: SP held the circling airspeed with the deviation settling at the 20 knot limit, due to an interrupted instrument cross-check while attention remained outside on the runway. The result is in line with the proficiency expected at this point of the syllabus. SP is expected to keep airspeed in the cross-check through the visual segment, not only the runway picture.
texts_at.2: SP held the circling airspeed with the deviation settling in the 10 to 20 knot band, due to a delayed power reduction after configuring the aircraft. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to reduce power the moment the aircraft is configured rather than a beat afterward.
texts_at.3: SP maintained the circling airspeed within 10 knots throughout the maneuvering, including through the configuration change and both turns, due to one power correction anticipated a fraction later than the others. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to anticipate every power correction with the same lead as the others.

texts_above.2: SP detected the trend on the next cross-check after the deviation reached the 10 to 20 knot band, adjusted power smoothly and re-established the target airspeed before the base turn, without prompting or intervention. Reducing power the moment the aircraft is configured, rather than a beat afterward, would keep that deviation smaller. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to sound power management in the circling pattern.
texts_above.3: SP maintained the circling airspeed within 10 knots throughout the maneuvering, including through the configuration change and both turns, with power corrections small and anticipated. The only refinement available is to anticipate every power correction with the same lead as the others. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to sure-handed power management in the circling pattern.
texts_above.4: SP flew the circling airspeed with negligible variation, well inside 10 knots at all points of the pattern, with airspeed remaining stable through the configuration change and both turns. There is little left to refine; every power adjustment is already minimal rather than corrective. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to exceptional power management in the circling pattern.

error_modes.label: Exit heading from circling turns and final alignment

texts.0: SP, due to an early and unassessed rollout from the base turn, did not exit the turn on the required heading for runway alignment. The aircraft rolled out more than 10 degrees off the extended runway centerline heading and the resulting overshoot could not be corrected with a normal turn. The IP intervened to re-align the aircraft with the runway.
texts.1: SP, due to an unmonitored bank angle in the turn to final, exited the turn at the 10 degree heading deviation limit. The misalignment was corrected only after the IP pointed out the offset, and the aircraft was re-aligned late in the final segment. No intervention on the controls was required.
texts.2: SP, due to a slightly late start of the turn to final, rolled out with a heading deviation in the 5 to 10 degree band from the runway heading. SP recognized the offset immediately, applied a coordinated correcting turn and was aligned with the runway well before the round out, without prompting or intervention.
texts.3: SP exited each circling turn within 5 degrees of the required heading and rolled out aligned with the extended runway centerline. Bank was adjusted during the turn so that the rollout required no additional correction.
texts.4: SP exited the circling turns with negligible heading error, rolling out essentially on the runway heading. Rate of turn was adjusted continuously so that alignment was achieved at rollout with no subsequent correction.
texts.marginal: SP met the heading standard on the exit from the turns, but the rollouts were repeatedly a few degrees to the outside of the runway heading and close to the 5 degree band. The trend is a late turn start compensated with increased bank at the end. SP is expected to select the turn point from a consistent visual reference so that the rollout heading is achieved without a final correction.

texts_at.1: SP exited the circling turns with the heading deviation settling at the 10 degree limit, due to an unmonitored bank angle in the turn to final. Performance remained inside the standard required for this stage of training. SP is expected to monitor bank angle continuously through the turn to final rather than only at roll-out.
texts_at.2: SP exited the circling turns with the heading deviation settling in the 5 to 10 degree band, due to a slightly late start of the turn to final. The result is in line with the proficiency expected at this point of the syllabus. SP is expected to start the turn to final at the same reference point on every approach.
texts_at.3: SP exited each circling turn within 5 degrees of the required heading and rolled out aligned with the extended runway centerline, due to bank adjusted a beat later than ideal during one turn. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to adjust bank at the start of every turn with the same timing as the others.

texts_above.2: SP recognized the offset immediately after the deviation settled in the 5 to 10 degree band, applied a coordinated correcting turn and was aligned with the runway well before the round out, without prompting or intervention. Starting the turn to final at the same reference point on every approach would keep that offset smaller. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to solid turn-exit technique.
texts_above.3: SP exited each circling turn within 5 degrees of the required heading and rolled out aligned with the extended runway centerline, with bank adjusted during the turn so the rollout required no additional correction. The only refinement available is to adjust bank at the start of every turn with the same timing as the others. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to well-developed turn-exit technique.
texts_above.4: SP exited the circling turns with negligible heading error, rolling out essentially on the runway heading with rate of turn adjusted continuously so alignment was achieved at rollout with no subsequent correction. There is little left to refine; every rollout is already exact rather than corrected into. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to outstanding turn-exit technique.

error_modes.label: Touch down point after the circling maneuver
error_modes.source: specific:TOUCH DOWN POINT (feet from the beginning of the RWY)

texts.0: SP, due to a high and fast final segment carried over from the circling maneuvering, did not control the aiming point and floated in the round out. Touch down occurred beyond 1500 feet from the beginning of the runway, the remaining runway was reduced below the briefed figure, and the IP intervened to complete the landing.
texts.1: SP, due to a shallow final flown without a fixed aiming point, arrived long and touched down at the 1500 foot limit from the beginning of the runway. The long touchdown was corrected only after the IP directed a power reduction and a positive descent to the runway, and recovery of the aiming point was late.
texts.2: SP, due to a slightly delayed power reduction in the round out, touched down in the 1000 to 1500 foot band from the beginning of the runway. SP recognized the developing float, reduced power and established a positive touchdown without prompting or intervention.
texts.3: SP controlled the final segment so that the aircraft touched down within 1000 feet of the beginning of the runway. The aiming point was established during the turn to final and the round out was completed without float.
texts.4: SP touched down consistently close to the planned aiming point and well inside 1000 feet from the beginning of the runway. Descent path and power were managed so that the round out required no correction and the touchdown occurred at the intended point.
texts.marginal: SP touched down within the standard, but the touchdown points were repeatedly near the 1000 foot figure and always on the long side. The trend is a slightly high final following the circling turn, absorbed by a longer float. SP is expected to fix the aiming point earlier and to reduce power at the round out so that touchdown occurs clearly inside the tighter figure.

texts_at.1: SP touched down with the point settling at the 1500 foot limit from the beginning of the runway, due to a shallow final flown without a fixed aiming point. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to fix the aiming point during the turn to final rather than flying the final shallow and unaimed.
texts_at.2: SP touched down with the point settling in the 1000 to 1500 foot band, due to a slightly delayed power reduction in the round out. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to reduce power at the round out the instant the float is recognized, not a moment after.
texts_at.3: SP controlled the final segment so the aircraft touched down within 1000 feet of the beginning of the runway, due to the aiming point being established a beat later than ideal during the turn to final. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to establish the aiming point at the same point in the turn as consistently as the others.

texts_above.2: SP recognized the developing float after the touchdown point trended into the 1000 to 1500 foot band, reduced power and established a positive touchdown without prompting or intervention. Reducing power at the round out the instant the float is recognized, rather than a moment after, would keep the touchdown point closer to the aim point. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to dependable aim-point technique.
texts_above.3: SP controlled the final segment so the aircraft touched down within 1000 feet of the beginning of the runway, with the aiming point established during the turn to final and the round out completed without float. The only refinement available is to establish the aiming point at the same point in the turn as consistently as the others. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to notably good aim-point technique.
texts_above.4: SP touched down consistently close to the planned aiming point and well inside 1000 feet, at about 700 feet from the beginning of the runway, with descent path and power managed so the round out required no correction. There is little left to refine; the touchdown point is already centered rather than long. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to superior aim-point technique.

error_modes.label: Deviation from runway centerline at touchdown

texts.0: SP, due to an uncorrected crosswind drift carried through the final segment, did not align the aircraft with the runway centerline. Lateral deviation at touchdown exceeded 15 feet with drift still present at contact, and the IP intervened on the controls to correct the alignment during the landing roll.
texts.1: SP, due to a wing low correction applied without reference to the centerline, touched down at the 15 foot lateral deviation limit. Alignment was corrected only after the IP called the drift, and the aircraft was returned to the centerline late in the landing roll. No intervention on the controls was required.
texts.2: SP, due to a late crosswind correction after rolling out from the circling turn, touched down with a lateral deviation in the 5 to 15 foot band. SP identified the offset before touchdown, applied rudder and aileron to align the aircraft and tracked back to the centerline immediately, with no prompting or intervention.
texts.3: SP touched down within 5 feet of the runway centerline with the aircraft aligned with the runway axis. Drift was canceled before touchdown and the landing roll was tracked on the centerline.
texts.4: SP touched down essentially on the runway centerline with negligible lateral offset and no drift at contact. Alignment was established during the turn to final and held through the round out and the landing roll.
texts.marginal: SP stayed within the lateral standard, but touchdowns were repeatedly on the same side of the centerline and near the 5 foot band. The trend is an incomplete drift correction carried out of the circling turn. SP is expected to establish the crosswind correction immediately at rollout on final and to hold the runway axis so that lateral offset stays clearly inside the tighter band.

texts_at.1: SP touched down with the lateral deviation settling at the 15 foot limit, due to a wing low correction applied without reference to the centerline. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to reference the centerline continuously while applying the wing low correction, not only at touchdown.
texts_at.2: SP touched down with the lateral deviation settling in the 5 to 15 foot band, due to a late crosswind correction after rolling out from the circling turn. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to apply the crosswind correction the instant the circling turn is complete rather than after rollout.
texts_at.3: SP touched down within 5 feet of the runway centerline with the aircraft aligned with the runway axis, due to drift canceled a beat later than ideal before touchdown. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to cancel drift at the same point in the round out on every landing.

texts_above.2: SP identified the offset before touchdown after the deviation reached the 5 to 15 foot band, applied rudder and aileron to align the aircraft and tracked back to the centerline immediately, without prompting or intervention. Applying the crosswind correction the instant the circling turn is complete, rather than after rollout, would keep that offset smaller. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to assured centerline discipline at touchdown.
texts_above.3: SP touched down within 5 feet of the runway centerline with the aircraft aligned with the runway axis, with drift canceled before touchdown and the landing roll tracked on the centerline. The only refinement available is to cancel drift at the same point in the round out on every landing. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to precise centerline discipline at touchdown.
texts_above.4: SP touched down essentially on the runway centerline with negligible lateral offset, about 2 feet, and no drift at contact, with alignment established during the turn to final and held through the round out and landing roll. There is little left to refine; alignment is already established before the round out rather than during it. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to first-rate centerline discipline at touchdown.

texts.0: SP, due to an uncontrolled airspeed decay in the round out after the circling turn, did not touch down within the required speed band. Touch down speed was more than 5 knots below the computed speed, the resulting sink rate was excessive, and the IP intervened with power and pitch to complete the landing.
texts.1: SP, due to excess airspeed carried from the final segment, touched down at the upper limit of the band, 10 knots above the computed touch down speed. The excess speed was reduced only after the IP directed a power reduction, and the round out was extended before the aircraft was placed on the runway.
texts.2: SP, due to a slightly late power reduction after rolling out on final, touched down 5 to 10 knots above the computed touch down speed. SP recognized the excess during the round out, reduced power and completed the touchdown without prompting or intervention.
texts.3: SP touched down within the required band, between the computed touch down speed and 5 knots above it. Power and pitch were managed through the round out so that the aircraft was placed on the runway at the correct attitude and speed.
texts.4: SP touched down essentially at the computed touch down speed with negligible excess. Deceleration through the round out was continuous and the aircraft was placed on the runway in the correct landing attitude.
texts.marginal: SP met the touch down speed standard, but the speeds were consistently at the top of the band, close to 5 knots above the computed figure. The trend is a fast final flown after the circling turn and not fully corrected before the round out. SP is expected to stabilize the approach speed before the round out so that touch down occurs closer to the computed speed.

texts_at.1: SP touched down with speed settling at the upper limit of the band, 10 knots above the computed touch down speed, due to excess airspeed carried from the final segment. Performance remained inside the standard required for this stage of training. SP is expected to stabilize the approach speed before the round out rather than carrying excess speed into it.
texts_at.2: SP touched down with speed settling 5 to 10 knots above the computed touch down speed, due to a slightly late power reduction after rolling out on final. The result is in line with the proficiency expected at this point of the syllabus. SP is expected to reduce power on rollout from the circling turn rather than partway down the final.
texts_at.3: SP touched down within the required band, between the computed touch down speed and 5 knots above it, due to the round out needing a beat longer than ideal to bleed the last of the excess speed. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to manage the round out so the last of the excess speed is bled off with the same timing as the rest of it.

texts_above.2: SP recognized the excess during the round out after speed settled 5 to 10 knots above the computed touch down speed, reduced power and completed the touchdown without prompting or intervention. Reducing power on rollout from the circling turn, rather than partway down the final, would remove most of that excess. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to competent speed management at touchdown.
texts_above.3: SP touched down within the required band, between the computed touch down speed and 5 knots above it, with power and pitch managed through the round out so the aircraft was placed on the runway at the correct attitude and speed. The only refinement available is to manage the round out so the last of the excess speed bleeds off with the same timing as the rest. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to disciplined speed management at touchdown.
texts_above.4: SP touched down essentially at the computed touch down speed with negligible excess, about 1 knot, with deceleration through the round out continuous and the aircraft placed on the runway in the correct landing attitude. There is little left to refine; the approach speed is already stabilized well before the round out. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to faultless speed management at touchdown.

error_modes.label: Standardized circling procedure and sequence of actions

texts.0: SP, due to incomplete knowledge of the circling procedure described in the Flight Manual and AFMAN 11-202 VOL3, did not execute the standardized sequence; the landing configuration and the associated checks were not completed in the prescribed order. The omission was not detected by SP and the approach was continued in an incorrect configuration. The IP intervened to complete the sequence and to keep the maneuver within the circling limits.
texts.1: SP, due to an uncertain recall of the circling sequence, did not carry out the required actions at the prescribed points; landing configuration and the associated checks were completed late in the maneuver. The sequence was completed only after verbal direction from the IP, and the delay compressed the remaining items on the base leg. No intervention on the controls was required.
texts.2: SP, due to a task order applied out of sequence when the circling clearance was received, initially omitted one item of the circling procedure. SP detected the omission on the downwind check, completed the item in time and re-established the standard flow without prompting or intervention.
texts.3: SP executed the circling approach according to the standardized procedure described in the Flight Manual and AFMAN 11-202 VOL3. Configuration, checks and the transition to the visual segment were completed at the correct points and in the correct order, without mistakes and without IP intervention.
texts.4: SP executed the circling procedure with no deviation from the standardized sequence and with the workload distributed evenly through the maneuver. Each action was completed at the correct point, leaving spare capacity for the visual segment and the landing.
texts.marginal: SP completed the circling procedure within standards, but several items were carried out at the latest acceptable point and the sequence had to be compressed on base. The trend is a reactive rather than an anticipated flow. SP is expected to complete the configuration and the checks earlier on the downwind so that the final segment is flown without concurrent procedural tasks.

texts_at.1: SP executed the standardized circling procedure with the landing configuration and checks completed only after being told point by point at the descent point, due to incomplete knowledge of the circling procedure described in the Flight Manual and AFMAN 11-202 VOL3. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to review the circling procedure sequence before the sortie so it is not reconstructed under IP direction.
texts_at.2: SP executed the standardized circling procedure with the required actions completed a few seconds later than the prescribed points, due to task order applied out of sequence when the circling clearance was received. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to hold the standardized order regardless of when the clearance is received.
texts_at.3: SP executed the circling approach according to the standardized procedure described in the Flight Manual and AFMAN 11-202 VOL3, due to one item completed at the latest usable point in the sequence rather than with margin ahead of it. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to give every item the same margin as the others rather than the latest usable point.

texts_above.2: SP detected the omission on the downwind check, completed the item in time and re-established the standard flow without prompting or intervention, after the task order had initially been applied out of sequence. Holding the standardized order regardless of when the clearance is received would prevent that omission from occurring. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to competent procedural discipline in the circling pattern.
texts_above.3: SP executed the circling approach according to the standardized procedure described in the Flight Manual and AFMAN 11-202 VOL3, with configuration, checks and the transition to the visual segment completed at the correct points and in the correct order. The only refinement available is to give every item the same margin as the others rather than the latest usable point. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to disciplined procedural execution in the circling pattern.
texts_above.4: SP executed the circling procedure with no deviation from the standardized sequence and with the workload distributed evenly through the maneuver, with each action completed at the correct point leaving spare capacity for the visual segment and the landing. There is little left to refine; the sequence already leaves spare capacity at every point. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to faultless procedural execution in the circling pattern.

error_modes.label: Circling minimum altitude and visual contact discipline

texts.0: SP, due to continuation bias in maintaining the approach after visual contact with the runway environment had become intermittent, descended below the published circling minimum altitude before the aircraft was in a position for a normal descent to landing. The minimum altitude was violated by more than 100 feet and the IP intervened to arrest the descent and to initiate the missed approach.
texts.1: SP, due to a decision to continue with a marginal visual reference, allowed the aircraft to reach the published circling minimum altitude with the descent still developing. The descent was arrested only after the IP directed a level off, and the decision on the missed approach was made late. No intervention on the controls was required.
texts.2: SP, due to an early start of the descent from the circling altitude in the base turn, approached the published minimum before the aircraft was in a position for a normal descent to landing. SP recognized the developing deviation, leveled at the circling altitude and continued the maneuver without prompting or intervention; the minimum was not violated.
texts.3: SP did not violate the circling minimum altitude at any point of the maneuver. The descent was initiated only when the aircraft was in a position from which a normal descent to landing could be made, with the runway environment continuously in sight.
texts.4: SP maintained the circling altitude precisely until the aircraft was in position for a normal descent to landing and never approached the published minimum. The descent point was identified early and stated, and visual contact with the runway environment was retained throughout the maneuver.
texts.marginal: SP did not violate the circling minimum, but the descent was initiated at the earliest defensible point and the margin to the published minimum was consistently small. The trend is an early descent started in the base turn. SP is expected to delay the descent until the normal descent path to landing is available so that a clear margin to the circling minimum is preserved.

texts_at.1: SP respected the circling minimum altitude with the decision to level off made only after the descent had reached the published minimum, due to a decision to continue with a marginal visual reference. Performance remained inside the standard required for this stage of training. SP is expected to make the level-off decision the instant the visual reference becomes marginal rather than continuing to assess it.
texts_at.2: SP respected the circling minimum altitude with the descent approaching the published minimum before it was leveled, due to an early start of the descent from the circling altitude in the base turn. The result is in line with the proficiency expected at this point of the syllabus. SP is expected to start the descent only when the aircraft is in a position for a normal descent to landing, not before.
texts_at.3: SP did not violate the circling minimum altitude at any point of the maneuver, with the descent initiated only when the aircraft was in a position from which a normal descent to landing could be made, due to that position being confirmed a beat later than ideal. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to confirm that position at the same point on every approach as consistently as the others.

texts_above.2: SP recognized the developing deviation, leveled at the circling altitude and continued the maneuver without prompting or intervention, after the descent had approached the published minimum before the aircraft was in position for a normal descent to landing. Starting the descent only when in position for a normal descent to landing, rather than before, would remove that margin. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to good judgement on the circling minimum.
texts_above.3: SP respected the circling minimum altitude throughout the maneuver, with the descent initiated only when the aircraft was in a position from which a normal descent to landing could be made and the runway environment continuously in sight. The only refinement available is to confirm that position with the same margin on every approach. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to very good judgement on the circling minimum.
texts_above.4: SP maintained the circling altitude precisely until the aircraft was in position for a normal descent to landing and never approached the published minimum, with the descent point identified early and stated and visual contact with the runway environment retained throughout. There is little left to refine; the descent point is already identified early rather than found in the maneuver. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to excellent judgement on the circling minimum.

texts.0: SP, due to a readback that was not compared with the clearance actually issued, did not follow the ATC circling directive and maneuvered on the opposite side of the runway to the one cleared. The deviation from the clearance was not recognized by SP and the IP intervened, taking control and coordinating the correction with ATC.
texts.1: SP, due to an incomplete listening watch while configuring the aircraft, did not comply with the ATC directive at the time given; the required report and the associated maneuver were both made late. Compliance was achieved only after the IP prompted SP and repeated the instruction. No intervention on the controls was required.
texts.2: SP, due to a partial readback of the circling clearance, initially began the maneuver in a manner that did not match the ATC directive. SP requested clarification, corrected the ground track and complied with the clearance promptly, without prompting or intervention.
texts.3: SP followed the ATC directives with precision, complying with the circling instruction and the assigned side of the runway. Readbacks were complete and accurate and the required reports were made at the correct points.
texts.4: SP anticipated and followed every ATC directive without error, with concise and complete readbacks. Reports were made at the correct points and the circling maneuver matched the clearance exactly, with no further instruction required from ATC.
texts.marginal: SP complied with all ATC directives, but readbacks were slow and one instruction had to be confirmed before it was actioned. The trend is a listening watch that degrades while cockpit tasks are in progress. SP is expected to keep the radio in the scan during configuration so that clearances are read back and executed without delay.

texts_at.1: SP followed the ATC circling directive with the maneuver initially begun in a manner that did not fully match the clearance before it was corrected, due to a partial readback of the circling clearance. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to confirm the full circling clearance before beginning the maneuver rather than after starting it.

texts.4: SP flew the MAIP circling pattern precisely, with consistent downwind spacing and turn points that produced a stabilized final without correction. SP maintained a clear picture of the aircraft position relative to the runway and to the protected area at all times.

error_modes.label: Insufficient downwind spacing leading to excessive bank in the turn to final

texts.2: SP, due to spacing that was set slightly tight for the wingtip reference, needed about 40 degrees of bank in the turn to final and initially overshot the extended centerline. error_modes.label: Excessive downwind spacing and the 1.5 NM obstacle clearance distance

error_modes.label: Rolling out wings level slower than the targeted final approach speed

texts.0: SP, due to failing to reduce airspeed from 120 KIAS progressively as bank was decreased in the turn to final, arrived at the roll-out with the speed still decaying towards the target for the flap setting. Airspeed passed more than 20 knots below the final approach speed appropriate for the configuration and the aircraft rolled out wings level slow and low on the glide-path. The IP intervened with power to restore the approach speed.
texts.1: SP, due to a power reduction made in one step instead of being matched to the decreasing bank, rolled out wings level 20 knots below the targeted final approach speed for the flap setting, at the deviation limit. texts.2: SP, due to reducing airspeed from 120 KIAS a little too early in the final turn, rolled out wings level between 10 and 20 knots below the targeted final approach speed.
